title: A steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP)-based BCI dataset in children and adolescents
description: EEG recordings from 47 neurotypical children and adolescents (5-18 years) who each completed a two-stage SSVEP-based brain-computer interface session. The session comprised a stimulus personalization pipeline followed by an online 4-target SSVEP game. Data were recorded with a 16-channel g.tec gel-based system at 256 Hz. The dataset was released by the BCI4Kids program to support signal-processing methods developed specifically for pediatric SSVEP-BCI data.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a g.tec g.GAMMAsys gel-based system (g.USBamp, g.GAMMAcap), 16 channels at 256 Hz, with earlobe reference and Fpz ground. Task T1 presented 12 stimuli (4 contrasts x 3 sizes) flickering at 10 Hz for personalization. Tasks T2 and T3 were an online 4-target SSVEP game at 6.25, 10, 11.11 and 14.28 Hz, played once with the personal stimulus and once with a high-contrast standard. Original XDF recordings were converted to BrainVision format with mne-bids.
